1.10: On macOS and Linux (ARM64 and 64-bit Intel/AMD), connect an Edision nano T265+ or another terrestrial TV receiver with HDMI output through a compatible USB capture device.
On Linux, confirm video and audio access from HDMI input. The Snap requires the camera and audio recording connections.
Open HDMI input in Live, choose the capture device’s video and audio, and scan or change channels using the receiver’s remote.
Record the HDMI input at up to 1080p with stereo sound or share it with your phone. The USB tuner still provides its own over-the-air features.
On macOS and Linux, Live adds picture modes and a personal setting for brightness, contrast, sharpness, and color.
1.9: Invisible TV · Signal analysis and Teletext
On macOS and Linux, explore the frequencies found during tuning as 3D planets. Zoom in to see their channels. A brighter marker identifies the live channel.
Select a channel to see real reception measurements and its video, audio, subtitle and teletext streams.
Data flows and Timeline show where the bitrate goes and what has changed in the broadcast.
The illustrated guide follows each tab, the channel picker groups channels by UHF, and the sidebar can be collapsed. Back to the universe restores the full map.
The active connection has round iridescent pulses. Data flows shows each type's share of the bitrate, and Channel anatomy groups the channel's streams.
Teletext on macOS and Linux adds a visual index for pages received over the air, with page numbers, a reading view and the original grid.
La 1 HD teletext loads automatically when the index arrives. The channel picker uses the same design and frequency groups as Signal analysis.
Teletext reading preserves broadcast accents, separates index columns and distinguishes page links from numbers in the text.
The expanded sidebar shows the green symbol and the Arkham TV name. The collapsed sidebar shows the symbol on its own.
1.8.24: Watch live TV on your phone
Open Watch on your phone and scan the QR code with an iPhone or Android device on the same Wi-Fi network.
Rotate your phone to expand the player. Use the full-screen button to reduce it or open the TV Guide to change the shared channel.
End mobile sharing from your computer. Channel changes from the phone are disabled during recording.
1.8.23: More DVB-T and DVB-T2 tuners on Ubuntu
Arkham TV detects DVB-T and DVB-T2 tuners that Ubuntu recognises. The AVerMedia A835 and A835B continue to support DVB-T.
The scan checks which standards the tuner supports. On a tuner that supports both, it tries DVB-T2 if there is no DVB-T signal on that frequency.
On Linux, the volume percentage is centred and stays the same width as the value changes.
1.8.22: Recordings can ride out brief encoder stalls without cutting out at startup or interrupting live playback.
If recording cannot keep up with the broadcast, Arkham TV shows a separate message from a signal loss.
1.8.21: On Ubuntu, the player checks that video advances when opening the app or switching channels and recovers automatically if the picture freezes.
Volume and mute are grouped in a compact module above the level meter that follows the current palette and appearance mode.
Saved channel lists can be deleted from the tuner. Your tuned channels remain available.
A counter shows how many TV channels the scan has found while it checks UHF frequencies.
Open your file manager from the recordings library or from an individual recording.
1.8.20: The Play or Pause button hides after three seconds of inactivity and reappears when you interact with the video.
1.8.19: If the picture freezes when switching channels, the player tries to recover automatically.
The player checks that video advances when opening a recording and retries if it stalls.
1.8.18: An illustration of Innsmouth harbor introduces Óscar Peña and Pedro Miñano, Arkham TV’s developer and beta tester and contributor.
1.8.17: The Play button retries playback if the player interrupts the initial load.
New recordings preserve audio and video synchronization in 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K.
1.8.16: Back to live TV and automatic channel playback
Live audio stops when you open Recordings. Return to Live to join the current broadcast.
Each channel starts playing when the video is ready. Sound is on at first launch and your mute preference is remembered.
The changelog credits Pedro Miñano as a beta tester and contributor.
1.8.15: Switch audio tracks from the player toolbar using the languages offered by each channel.
Choose a stereo audio track and record in 4K, 1080p, 720p or 480p. The same options are available for live and TV Guide recordings.
1.8.14: Synchronized audio displays, programme details and local time
The level meter and audio spectrum follow the audio being played, including in the mini player.
Programme cards separate the synopsis, broadcast details and credits supplied by each channel.
The Live page shows a 24-hour local clock below the language selector.
1.8.13: Recordings are saved in 1080p at a constant frame rate with stereo AAC audio. Main programme audio takes priority over audio description.
Ubuntu builds accelerate video processing on ARM64 and Intel. The folder picker lets you browse, create a folder and choose where to save recordings.
The audio sync selector matches the language menu, marks the selected channel and tells you when no channels have been tuned yet.
1.8.12: A language menu that matches the app
The language menu follows the Arkham TV theme, marks the active language and can be opened and dismissed with the keyboard.
1.8.11: English and Spanish, with clearer channel quality
Switch between Spanish and English from the top bar. The player, guide, settings and changelog follow your choice.
Channel cards use SD, HD and UHD for the received resolution and show the measured size. The badge explains when it differs from the format advertised in the channel name.
1.8.10: Clearer text and first launch on Snap
The bundled typeface keeps text aligned with icons. Headings have more breathing room, and the Snap shows channel logos on cards again.
The Snap includes the codecs and opens its native Ubuntu window without requiring a separate library installation.
1.8.9: The Ubuntu edition opens correctly on systems with both GTK 3 and GTK 4. The package installs the required libraries.
1.8.8: The macOS About panel updates the developer credit and describes tuning, playback, recording and compatibility.
1.8.7: New cards and easier access to the changelog
Channel cards give the logo, name and frequency more room. The Arkham TV octopus appears as a watermark, and a legend identifies SD, HD and UHD.
A bookmark replaces the star. Drag cards into Favourites or reorder them within the list.
Arkham TV saves detected video resolution and fixes damaged characters in names such as SX3/33 and La Séptima, including saved lists.
The changelog has an icon at the bottom of the sidebar. Its header credits the developer and opens without an outline around the title.
1.8.6: An HH:MM:SS timer below the video shows how long the recording has been running.
Play saved files in the main window with a Recording badge, or delete them from the library.
Minimizing the app moves live playback to a floating window with the channel, programme and audio spectrum.
New location moves to the left of the UHF range and scan controls, making the tuner panel shorter.
The footer links to the changelog, with the history of Arkham TV back to version 1.0.
1.8.5: New location is easier to spot, and Scan from scratch explains what the next scan will do.
1.8.4: Record from the player or schedule a recording from the TV Guide. MP4 files are saved at 1080p in the folder you choose, with the title and date.
During a scheduled recording you can watch another channel on the same UHF frequency. Manual recordings stop when you change channel.
Save and load named lists for home, hotels or a portable antenna. The status indicator distinguishes antenna reception from the USB connection.
The vector logo retains transparency and adapts to light and dark mode.
1.8.3: The synopsis separates the plot from credits, even in compact descriptions from channels such as Cuatro and Be Mad.
Arkham TV verifies the OMDb key and looks up films when you open the programme card. You can choose the correct title if several results match.
1.8.2: An antenna icon indicates tuner status and has more space between it and the Appearance button.
1.8.1: Readable synopses and pasting on macOS
Programme cards separate the synopsis from the original title, director, cast and other broadcast information.
The macOS Edit menu lets you paste an OMDb key from another app using ⌘V.
1.8.0: An expandable card below the video shows the programme, schedule, progress and synopsis. You can look up films on IMDb and get more details from OMDb.
The footer automatically identifies the connected tuner model.
1.7.2: Steadier volume control and updated branding
The volume slider stays in place while you drag it, and the mute button keeps its width when toggled.
The app logo and icon have been updated.
1.7.1: A segmented bar display follows the energy in ten frequency bands, from 31 Hz to 16 kHz.
The footer identifies DVB-T compatibility with AVerMedia A835 and A835B.
1.7.0: A channel grid shows the schedule received over the antenna and lets you tune from a programme card.
A ten-band equalizer, presets such as Dialogue, Cinema, Night and Rock, and digital or analogue stereo meters. The active preset and curve are shown on the live page.
In full screen, the sound control hides after five seconds and reappears when you move the pointer.
Favourites move to a row below the live stream, before the channel catalogue.
macOS and Ubuntu use the same version numbers.
1.6.4: On macOS, per-channel audio sync can correct voices that come before or after the picture.
About Arkham TV lists the developer credit and macOS compatibility separately.
1.6.3: Ubuntu recognizes the A835B with USB ID 07ca:3835 as well as the A835. Setup installs the firmware required by the IT9135 variant.
1.6.2: The .deb packages install a launcher with the octopus icon, include FFmpeg and FFprobe, and list WebKitGTK and codecs as dependencies.
1.6.1: The native window checks for H.264 codecs, and playback in Parallels has been adjusted to prevent a black screen.
1.6: Ubuntu Intel and ARM64 editions open in their own GTK window with WebKitGTK.
1.5: Portable Intel and ARM64 executables launch a browser interface and support the A835 and Volar HD PRO family.
1.4.1: An interface that adapts to the window
Video keeps its aspect ratio as the window is resized. Audio sync fields and buttons share the same height.
The horizontal volume slider uses the same green as the full screen control and responds better to dragging.
1.4: Settings lets you delay audio when voices play ahead of the picture and saves the offset for the next session.
1.3: Channel logos and controls below the video
More national channel logos are matched by name, including HD variants. The macOS title is centred and the footer shows the version.
The horizontal volume slider sits next to Mute below the video. The full screen control remains vertical.
1.2: Save favourites by dragging channels into the area or clicking the star. The footer credits the developer.
The full screen volume control becomes vertical and moves to the lower right.
1.1: Arkham TV comes to the Mac desktop
The universal app for Intel and Apple Silicon includes firmware and playback tools. It scans for or restores channels at launch.
The design adds the octopus icon, light and dark palettes, shortcuts to Channels and Tuner, and channel logos.
The player lets you mute and unmute sound.
1.0: The local web app tunes terrestrial TV with the AVerMedia A835 on macOS, scans UHF frequencies and filters channels by name.
The player shows live antenna broadcasts and supports full screen.
